source_file: 10193115_2024_Mills Pond Group LLC v. Town of Smithtown, New York_nyed
notes: FHA claim dismissed on ripeness/standing grounds; court did not reach merits of disability-discrimination theory.
Complaint survived Section 1915 screening; court found plausible FHA disability claim plead.
FHA claim failed because plaintiff did not tie alleged mistreatment to disability as opposed to other characteristics.
Court found no facts suggesting disability was motivating factor for adverse action.
Complaint did not tie conduct to disability; failed to connect alleged harm to protected class.
Court found disability not properly alleged with facts showing substantial limitation of major life activity.
FHA retaliation claim failed because plaintiff did not adequately plead causation between protected activity and adverse action.
Court lacked subject matter jurisdiction; McCarran-Ferguson Act reverse-preemption of FHA insurance claim.

source_file: 10670447_2025_Olley v. TodmanThe clerks office is ORDERED to not accept any further filings in this matter until the motions to dismiss are ruled on.._txsd
notes: Multiple procedural defects including sovereign immunity and Monell deficiencies; court did not reach merits.

source_file: 10708675_2025_J. F. and on behalf of her adolescents and mother v. LUIS VENTURA_txnd
notes: Multiple independent defects analyzed including standing, disability not adequately pleaded, and element gaps.

source_file: 10745833_2025_Mekal Faruki v. Housing Authority for the County of Sacramento, et al._caed
notes: Court found comparator (friend) was also disabled, so differential treatment did not plausibly suggest disability discrimination.

source_file: 10776210_2026_Bolima Tafah et al. v. Lake Village Townhomes et al._mdd
notes: Conclusory allegations without supporting factual detail; pleading insufficient under Iqbal/Twombly.

source_file: 11267550 - Pella v. ATLANTIC COUNTY DEPARTMENT OF FAMILY AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT
notes: Court found EA benefits administration is not conduct covered by FHA's rental/sale provisions.

source_file: 11267625 - Jones v. FEATHERSTONE CONDOMINIUM HOMEOWNERS ASSOCIATION INC.
notes: Retaliation claim failed for lack of adverse action; failure-to-accommodate claim failed because plaintiff did not identify disability or explain necessity.

source_file: 7235405_2016_Louis ex rel. G.A.H. v. New York City Housing Authority_nysd
notes: Court found Section 8 program benefits do not include housing provision or modifications; requested accommodations would substantively alter benefits.
Court found disability not adequately pleaded as substantial limitation on major life activity AND plaintiff did not allege requested accommodation.
Court found requested accommodation (turn off cell tower) was not reasonable; T-Mobile not subject to FHA for non-rental/sale conduct.

source_file: 9639620_2020_Cobb v. Citrus Falls at Westchase Apartments, LLC_flmd
notes: Court found structural improvements and defective-construction claims do not fit within Section 3604(f)(3)(B) reasonable accommodation framework.
Plaintiff alleged habitability issues (mold/heat) but did not plead protected-class discrimination; no cognizable FHA theory.

source_file: 9725785_2022_Discovery Real Estate and Development, LLC v. Town of St. Francisville_lamd
notes: FHA claim dismissed for lack of standing and ripeness; sewer moratorium made harm non-traceable and non-redressable.
Plaintiff failed to identify disability or factually tie alleged adverse actions to any protected characteristic.
Dismissed under Rooker-Feldman doctrine for lack of subject-matter jurisdiction over challenge to state-court eviction.
District court order accepting R&R dismissed FHA disability claim without prejudice with leave to amend; underlying R&R reasoning not in opinion text.
Court found no facts suggesting FHA-protected discrimination or retaliation; Section 8 termination claim does not state FHA claim without protected-class nexus.

source_file: 9876248_2022_Sykes v. New York City Housing Authority_nysd
notes: Court found no facts showing disability was motivating factor for failure to repair; also lack of notice/request for accommodation.
Court found plaintiff failed to plead that defendants knew of his disability or that he requested an accommodation tied to the disability.
Court found plaintiff stated prima facie FHA failure-to-accommodate claim but dismissed as time-barred by 2-year FHA statute of limitations.

source_file: 9936025_2022_HONKALA v. U.S. DEPARTMENT OF HOUSING _ URBAN DEVELOPMENT_paed
notes: Court found plaintiffs not 'buyers or renters' within meaning of FHA; squatters occupying PHA property without consideration have no FHA claim.
Court found sale of handicap parking spaces not itself FHA violation absent alternative access, plus plaintiff never requested accommodation and defendant had no knowledge of her disability.
Court found complaint 'makes no connection between any act of defendants and plaintiff's impairments'; no disability nexus to broken-door grievance.
